- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak in early periods (first 5–7 days); model tends to lag by 1–2 days; adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days if recent price is trending down.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.2–0.7); apply a “sentiment-weighted adjustment” — add 0.5–1.5% for sentiment >0.5, subtract 0.5–1.5% for sentiment <0.5.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.8 → 0.0 → 0.8), model fails to anticipate reversal; reduce forecast 1–2 days before reversal signal.
